scope: Actual staged v1/v2 TypeScript classes, independently instantiated from the same candidate glue/WASM. Real caller allocation and codec-output ownership measured through a Module Proxy; only bounded JS exceptions and one mocked null allocation are injected.
boundaries: No real OOM, allocator corruption, invalid free, arbitrary pointer, trap, browser, worker, full application, GPU or production packaging claim.
Unowned frees are refused by the harness before reaching real WASM. Failed-case emergency cleanup never changes the recorded failing result.
Counters cover caller-visible allocation/free and outputs from real codec returns, not every internal libwebp allocation.
v1/v2 equality uses the same binary. It proves cleanup preserves successful output; default exact=0 may still change RGB under fully transparent pixels relative to input.
The production baseline harness and license/public/app resources are not modified.
